newsitem.title: UK: BZW launches UK property market derivative.
newsitem.headline: BZW launches UK property market derivative.

text.p: BZW, the investment banking arm of British banking giant Barclays Plc, said on Friday it had launched a property market derivative.

"The new instrument, BZW Property Index Forwards (PIFs), which began trading today, is a simple, understandable structure, designed to appeal to the widest possible range of property market participants," BZW Property Investment Management and BZW Global Markets Division said in a statement.
The instruments are designed for institutional investors and are meant to encourage liquidity, they added.

The PIFs are contracts for differences which are based on the level of a commercial property market index, the "Investment Property Databank" (IPD). This covers around 80 percent of institutionally held property in the UK, represents all sectors and regions, and is currently valued at around 47 billion stg.

If the index is higher at expiry date than the agreed forward price, then the holder of a long position in a PIF will receive money but if the index is less than the agreed forward price then the holder of a long position would pay money.

Settlement is a cash payment between Barclays and the client. "The transaction is analogous to buying a portfolio of property at the agreed forwards price and then selling at the index level at the expiry date, thereby realising a profit or a loss," BZW said.

BZW said the PIFs will be launched with expiry dates of December 1997 and December 1998. Barclays Plc will act as counterparty for all transactions, it will provide liquidity support to the market and indicate bid and offer prices on Reuters screens, BZW said.

"PIFs will provide price transparency not yet seen in the property market, with the price of a forward contract determined by supply and demand," said Ian Reid, chief executive of BZW Property Investment Management.
"They are likely to be used as a tactical play, by providing clients with the ability to increase (long position) or decrease (short position) exposure levesl quickly and cheaply," he added.
